sources.title: Sonar Reasoning Pro — legacy model reference
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026 through the Markdown endpoint. Exact legacy model card gives 128K context, Chain-of-Thought reasoning, enhanced retrieval and cited text answers, with an image-input/structured-output warning. It gives no parameter count or backbone name; the earlier archived developer model overview supplies that lineage (s19). Retained legacy documentation does not establish current backend operation.

sources.evidence: Lists Sonar Reasoning Pro within the Sonar range, distinct from Sonar Pro and Sonar Deep Research.

sources.title: Improved Sonar Models: Industry Leading Performance at Lower Costs
sources.evidence: March 19, 2025 article names Sonar Reasoning Pro among updated models and changes search effort and pricing; it refers to existing usage and does not establish the original release.

sources.title: API changelog
sources.evidence: March 2025 search-mode update includes Reasoning Pro; April 2025 adds Sonar image uploads. November 2025 automated web_search/fetch_url_content announcement specifically concerns Sonar Pro, not Reasoning Pro. December 15, 2025 retirement concerns sonar-reasoning without Pro.

sources.title: Migrate from Sonar — overview
sources.evidence: Sonar Chat Completions support ended September 27, 2026. Synchronous/streaming compatibility requests are gradually reformulated as Agent API requests; this does not prove continued use of the original Reasoning Pro backend.

sources.title: Perplexity API Terms of Service
sources.evidence: January 23, 2026 terms cover Sonar API services. Sections 2.1 and 3.1 grant restricted service use and reserve service/model IP to Perplexity or licensors; support proprietary hosted-service classification, not an open-weight license.

sources.title: Media & Attachments — legacy Sonar API
sources.evidence: Legacy API guide documents image input alongside text and text responses. Code examples use sonar-pro; this guide alone cannot establish exact Reasoning Pro support. Read with the exact model card image-input caveat.

sources.title: Efficient and Portable Mixture-of-Experts Communication
sources.evidence: First-party communication-kernel research was reviewed for architecture disclosures. It does not identify Sonar Reasoning Pro or supply a model-specific parameter table.

sources.title: Lower Latency and Higher Throughput with Multi-node DeepSeek Deployment
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. Perplexity states DeepSeek-V3/R1 have nominal 671B total and 37B activated parameters, with MoE and Multi-Latent Attention. The article itself does not name Sonar Reasoning Pro, but its R1 specifications corroborate DeepSeek’s official card (s20); the missing exact-model R1 binding is now recovered from Perplexity’s archived model overview (s19).

sources.title: RL Training For Math Reasoning
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. First-party RL research discusses experiments using Llama 3.1 8B base/instruct and R1-generated training data. It does not identify Sonar Reasoning Pro or disclose a structural modification to its documented R1 backbone.

sources.title: Accelerating Sonar Through Speculation
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. Discusses Sonar acceleration with an in-house Llama-1B draft, MTP heads, and DeepSeek-scale inference. Does not name Sonar Reasoning Pro. Auxiliary draft or MTP parameters are not added to the nominal R1 backbone count or treated as grounds for discarding it.

sources.title: R1-1776 official model repository
sources.evidence: Repository and raw README previously returned HTTP 401; the raw README returned HTTP 401 again on October 27, 2026. No R1-1776-to-Reasoning-Pro identity is inferred from inaccessible material; the independently recovered first-party binding is to DeepSeek R1 (s19).

sources.title: Sonar Reasoning Pro provider endpoint metadata
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. Distributor metadata describes this exact model as powered by DeepSeek R1, with text/image input, text output and 128000 context. Its R1 claim is now corroborated by archived Perplexity documentation (s19), rather than serving as the sole lineage basis. The March 7, 2025 created timestamp remains a later listing; conflicting tool flags are not proof of model-selected tool use.

sources.title: Contemporaneous Sonar Reasoning Pro discussion and documentation screenshots
sources.publisher: LINUX DO user Twilight9; reproduced Perplexity documentation
sources.evidence: February 3, 2025 post preserves two screenshots, both visually inspected: supported-model and pricing tables already list sonar-reasoning-pro separately. The screenshots have no publisher date or announcement; this establishes an earlier availability lead, not a verified first release day/month.

sources.title: Sonar Reasoning Pro model analysis
sources.evidence: Third-party page claims January 28, 2025 release. This conflicts with other catalog dates and lacks a recovered original developer release announcement; retained only as an unresolved chronology lead.

sources.title: Sonar Now Supports Image Upload
sources.evidence: Staff announcement dated April 16, 2025 says Sonar now accepts image uploads. It does not enumerate model variants; used as general rollout context, not independent exact-variant proof.

sources.title: Models.dev Sonar Reasoning Pro record
sources.evidence: Original catalog source was inspected. It asserts January 1, 2024, tool_call=false and text/image input without primary release evidence; it is not verification of those assertions.

sources.title: Perplexity Sonar Dominates New Search Arena Evaluation
sources.evidence: April 14, 2025 article directly names Sonar Reasoning Pro and Sonar Reasoning as distinct reasoning models. It reports search evaluation, not parameter counts, architecture or original release timing.

sources.title: Perplexity Models — April 5, 2025 archived developer documentation
sources.evidence: Freshly recovered and read October 27, 2026. The rendered Reasoning Models section explicitly lists sonar-reasoning-pro as “Premier reasoning offering powered by DeepSeek R1 with Chain of Thought (CoT).” It separately lists the offline r1-1776 model. This is direct developer identification of the reasoning backbone, not merely OpenRouter attribution. No pruning, distillation, expert expansion or other architecture-changing modification is described. The supported nominal backbone specification is historical; the page does not name an exact fine-tuned checkpoint.

sources.title: DeepSeek-R1 official model card — nominal total and activated parameters
sources.evidence: Read October 27, 2026. Model Downloads table reports DeepSeek-R1 with 671B total and 37B activated parameters; the evaluation table explicitly classifies R1 as MoE, and the card identifies DeepSeek-V3-Base ancestry. The separately listed R1-Distill checkpoints are not the named DeepSeek-R1 backbone. Use these published nominal specifications, not the repository’s aggregate 684B tensor-size display. Combined with s19 this supports a labeled inference for Sonar Reasoning Pro’s historical language backbone.

sources.title: Sonar Reasoning Pro — August 1, 2025 archived exact-model documentation
sources.evidence: Freshly read October 27, 2026 to check later exact-model documentation for superseding architecture or size disclosures. Describes advanced multi-step reasoning, enhanced retrieval, 128K context and twice the search results of Sonar Reasoning, without a new parameter count, a different backbone or a stated structural change. This omission does not retract the earlier explicit R1 identification.

name.note: Exact public model name and API identifier sonar-reasoning-pro.

developer.note: Perplexity publishes and supplies this named API model.

family.note: Normalize to the documented Sonar range; reasoning is a capability subgroup.

release_date.note: Clear unsupported 2024-01-01. January 28 is an unverified third-party claim; a February 3 post reproduces an already-listed model; March 7 is OpenRouter listing and March 19 is a developer update. Searches for the original Perplexity/CEO announcement did not recover an exact-variant launch post. Neither first day nor month is securely established.

open_weights.note: This record describes Perplexity's proprietary hosted Sonar service, not a downloadable checkpoint. An upstream open-weight model would not make the service itself open weights.

license.note: Descriptive classification for the hosted model under Perplexity API terms. No MIT license is inherited from an asserted R1 ancestor.

parameters_b.note: Nominal historical language-backbone total inferred from explicit developer lineage: Perplexity’s April 5, 2025 archived model overview identifies sonar-reasoning-pro as powered by DeepSeek R1; DeepSeek publishes 671B total for R1. Reviewed later exact-model and research material discloses no pruning, distillation, expert expansion or replacement that defeats this inference. The exact fine-tuned checkpoint and later service backend remain unspecified, but an exact tensor census is not required to retain this supported nominal specification. Accept with proposed language_backbone scope; do not interpret it as all hosted-service components.

active_parameters_b.note: Nominal 37B activated parameters per token for the historically identified DeepSeek-R1 language backbone, supported separately by DeepSeek’s total/activated table and Perplexity’s deployment article. This is not inferred by equating active with total. The exact served checkpoint, batch-wide union of activated experts, speculative draft and auxiliary retrieval/vision components are outside this per-token backbone figure. Accept with proposed language_backbone scope.

architecture.note: Historical language-backbone architecture inferred from Perplexity’s explicit DeepSeek R1 identification. DeepSeek’s model card identifies R1 as MoE, corroborated by Perplexity’s deployment research. This does not specify auxiliary image-processing components, an exact fine-tuned checkpoint, or a later Agent API backend.

context_window.note: Last documented 128K; distributor corroborates decimal 128000. Earlier reproduced docs show 127K. Retain the later legacy limit, without asserting current backend behavior.

modalities.note: Retain documented API-level text/image input and text output. Exact card specifically restricts image input combined with structured outputs, consistent with the legacy media guide and distributor metadata. Does not establish a natively multimodal backbone or image generation.

reasoning.note: Explicit Chain-of-Thought capability; exact response example includes a thinking section.

tool_call.note: Clear blanket false. Retrieval and citations are established, but reviewed exact-model evidence does not establish model-selected tool invocation or custom function calling. November Pro Search tool orchestration is explicitly Sonar Pro; it is not borrowed. Conflicting distributor tool flags do not resolve the issue.

patch.notes: Original release timing remains unresolved: the 2024-01-01 catalog date is unsupported; January 28, 2025 is a third-party claim, February 3 documentation screenshots show earlier availability than the March 7 OpenRouter listing, and March 19 was an update. The 128K context and image-input restrictions describe the legacy service. Sonar Chat Completions support ended September 27, 2026; compatibility requests are gradually reformulated through Agent API, so successful requests do not verify the original backend. Fresh October 27 parameter re-audit recovered an April 5, 2025 archive of Perplexity’s own model overview explicitly identifying sonar-reasoning-pro as powered by DeepSeek R1. DeepSeek’s official card and Perplexity’s deployment research establish the nominal R1 specifications of 671B total, 37B activated per token and MoE architecture. Retain those as a documented lineage inference for the historical language backbone, together with the proposed component and active scopes; no reviewed primary source discloses structural changes defeating the inference. Exact fine-tuned checkpoint, later backend revisions and auxiliary search, routing, image-processing or speculative-decoding components remain unspecified and are not counted. Missing exact deployed tensor sizes do not invalidate the nominal backbone specification. Tool invocation remains unverified; built-in retrieval alone does not establish model-selected tools, and Sonar Pro’s Pro Search capabilities are not inherited.

summary: Fresh October 27 parameter re-audit recovered archived first-party documentation explicitly tying Sonar Reasoning Pro to DeepSeek R1. Restore nominal 671B total and 37B activated per token, with MoE architecture, as historical language-backbone specifications inferred from that developer binding and the official R1 card. Accept these values with the proposed component and active scopes. The exact fine-tuned checkpoint, auxiliary components and later backend remain unspecified; original release timing and model-selected tool support remain unresolved. Other audited fields are preserved.
